page: Microsoft Azure D128pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance from the Dplsv7 family, provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 128 dedicated 64-bit ARM (arm64) vCPUs coupled with 256.0 GB of system memory, producing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server contains no onboard graphics processors and features no local instance storage, requiring persistent data to be attached via external Premium Storage volumes.

Configured with a low-memory density profile, the D128pls_v7 prioritizes core counts over per-thread memory footprint. The dedicated ARM architecture delivers compute efficiency for highly parallelized execution, reducing memory overhead costs relative to balanced 1:4 profiles. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local temporary NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O depends on network-attached storage infrastructure. Additionally, x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX and AMX are not supported on this arm64 configuration.

With its 128 dedicated ARM cores and 256 GB of memory, this server is structured for horizontally scaled, CPU-heavy tasks that do not demand extensive memory allocations per process. Suitable workloads include continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) build farms, parallel batch processing, microservice container clusters, and scalable web serving environments compiled for ARM64 platforms.
description: Microsoft Azure D128pls_v7 is an ARM64-based virtual machine within the Dplsv7 family, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is configured with 128 dedicated ARM vCPUs and 256.0 GB of memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local physical storage, relying entirely on remote Premium Storage options for persistent disk operations. With its 1:2 processor-to-memory ratio, the configuration is positioned for high-density compute tasks that require extensive parallel threading without heavy per-core memory demands. Because it uses the ARM architecture, x86-specific extensions are unsupported, requiring software built for 64-bit ARM platforms. The server delivers qualitative resource efficiency for parallelized processing where dedicated multi-core capacity is prioritized. Suitable deployment targets include continuous integration pipelines, batch data transformations, multi-threaded microservice fabrics, and large-scale web serving fleets that operate across arm64 runtimes.
